articleTitle: The resilience of critical power infrastructures within National Power Grid in order to prevent a black-out and ensure energy security
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: “Black-out” is a total lack of power for all consumers (domestic, industrial and critical) and can cause multiple damage to industry and national economy. Because power infrastructure by power sub/stations and overhead power lines ensures access to electricity for consumers, it is critical that all sectors of the industrial economy are dependent on electricity and European Union must ensure their protection for resilience. If protection measures are not carried out, critical power infrastructure may become vulnerable. The authors consider that the analysis and quantification of a black-out, the identification of critical power infrastructures, the conceptualization of critical infrastructures and resilience are elements of novelty brought to the work.

articleTitle: Design and Development of SP Hybrid Manufacturing Prototype combining 3D printing and CNC Milling
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Nowadays the most two crucial procedures utilized to create parts used as a prototype are rapid prototyping (RP) and the classical methods of CNC manufacturing. Rapid prototyping (RP) creates rapidly a physical part directly from its CAD model data using various manufacturing techniques. Rapid prototyping can be used at any stage of the product development cycle for any components or sub-components. The CNC is often used to create parts by material removal as a subtractive technology. The main limitation of this technology is related to the possibility of manufacturing very complex parts. The focus of this paper is twofold. Firstly, it aims to combine two well-known technologies to provide an easier way to manufacture complex parts. Secondly, it aims to improve the surface finish and achieve high accuracy very close to the CAD model. For this case study, it was designed a new prototype of hybrid manufacturing which is using fuse deposition modeling (FDM) equipment to print the material. Also, CNC milling equipment to remove the excess material. Both subassembly tools were displaced on the same X-axis. By developing the new manufacturing prototype, we aimed to solve some of the limitations related to the quality of the final part. We targeted to improve the surface finish of the parts and to assure the required geometrical tolerance, The validation of the new prototype is made by comparing the results with existing ones from other researchers. All the steps that were followed starting from the design to the execution phase will be presented.

articleTitle: Application of feedback linearization method to wind turbines with PMSG for extracting maximum power from wind energy
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In this paper it is proposed a state feedback linearization method for a wind turbine equipped with a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG), in order to extract maximum power from wind energy. The method is based on Lie derivatives and has several advantages as: adjusting the power coefficient of wind turbine as close as possible to its maximum value, obtaining the optimal tip speed ratio of wind turbine, along with maintaining the generator speed at optimum value. For the state linearized feedback controller design (determining the parameters vector) it was used the pole-placement method. For the classic maximum power point tracking (MPPT) control structure, a PI controller is synthesized with the Matlab PIDtune program. For wind turbine with PMSG of 2 MW, based on the model built in Matlab, the results obtained with state feedback linearization method are presented. These results are compared with those obtained with the classic MPPT control structure.

articleTitle: Computation of Street Lighting in High-Risk Areas. Part I. Ramped Roads
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Since it can greatly lower the risk of accidents for both vehicles and pedestrians, street lighting is essential for high-risk areas. This two-part paper presents in-depth analyses of street lighting in all those critical circumstances where surface illumination must be provided in a non-conventional manner, such as roads with varying degrees of inclination or curvature, or areas in crossroads or roundabouts. Comprehensive case studies were conducted for each of these situations. These were accomplished through simulations run through the DIAlux evo software. The same initial conditions were considered in each case, and some elements, such as the road's gradient of ramps or the degree or the radius of curvature for the analysis of illumination in curves, were modified. All the obtained results were compared with a set of reference results obtained for a custom case which consisted of using standardized characteristics to improve the light on a road section. This case was used as a reference.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a multi-battery, multi-chemistry state of health screening system
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Considering the growing demand for electric mobility, the need for cost-effective and fast state of health screening systems have to be addressed. The State of Health of a battery is a key indicator of its performance and safety, and the parameters that correlate with it are battery capacity and internal resistance. A proposed solution for a portable, multi-chemistry and multi-battery state of health screening system with digital control is validated using Matlab/Simulink program by modeling batteries with real data. The determination of internal resistance takes 18 seconds, and the proposed system allows testing two cells at the same time, reducing the overall operational time in half.

articleTitle: The influence of insulation active power losses on the single line-to-ground fault in medium voltage electrical networks with resonant grounding
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Power delivery at medium voltage level over an ever-expanding electrical grid is more prone to faults than at other higher voltage level. The most common fault type in these electrical networks is the single line-to-ground fault. It is therefore necessary to design protection schemes that ensure a fast and selective detection of such faults. A reliable operation of the protective relays depends on the accurate analytical computation of the single line-to-ground fault current. This paper tackles a key issue of long-term scenario planning, namely the influence of the medium voltage distribution network insulation state on the fault current and on the medium voltage busbars zero-sequence voltage based on which the protective relays make a discriminatory decision when such a fault occurs. The purpose of this paper is to emphasise that the setting of these relays must be reviewed periodically and updated according to the latest insulation strength parameters values.

articleTitle: Experimental validation of simulation models for the emitter coil of an WPT system
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This article investigates the magnetic field distribution generated by the emitter coil of a Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) system, in two ways, through simulation and experimental measurement. More exactly, a comparative analysis is made in several relevant points from the selected 2D plans through the center of the coil. Data captured from perpendicular vertical XZ plane and YZ respectively, were used as reference values. For the investigations, a commercial double planar coil was considered as device under test (DUT). In both investigations, simulated and measured, the same initial conditions were considered, for the current density of the coil materials and for its geometric dimensions. Experimental values of magnetic field distribution were captured with a high-resolution measurement system developed in the laboratory. Finally, the simulated result of magnetic field distribution for considered emitter coil were compared with measurements of the real product. The profile of the simulated field in the selected plans overlaps the profile of the field distribution from measurements. Also, the standard deviation errors are presented in the results section. General conclusions were formulated based on the comparison results.

articleTitle: Voltage Control in Electric Networks with Wind Farms Connected Using a Scenario-Based Optimization Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: A scenario-based optimization framework associated with voltage control in the electric networks with wind farms connected has been proposed in the paper. The optimization process corresponds to the Optimal Power Flow (OPF) problem, where the reduced gradient method, characterized by a fast convergence (few iterations), has been used. The proposed framework allows the network operator to maintain a constant voltage level in the nodes and reduce energy losses. Testing in a test 10-bus network demonstrated the efficiency of the proposed framework for all considered scenarios referring to the generation profiles and the operating regimes of two wind farms connected. The results revealed the high potential of the proposed framework to help the network operators in the voltage control from the electric networks with wind farms connected, mitigating the voltage variations at the buses from values located in the range [0.05, 0.09] p.u. to [0.004, 0.007] p.u. and also highlighted the advantages of this approach in reducing energy losses quantified through the energy-savings with values between 18% and 42% compared with the initial operating regime.

articleTitle: Analysis and simulation of a hybrid energy system using HOMER Pro for TUCN blocks of buildings *Note: Sub-titles are not captured in Xplore and should not be used
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The main objective of this paper is to study the integration of renewable energy sources in a block of buildings of the Technical University of Cluj-Napoca (TUCN), to reduce consumption costs. Feasibility studies and analysis will be carried out, having as technical application the design of a hybrid energy system with renewable sources, covering as much as possible of the total electricity demand. A 4kW photovoltaic system (PV) is already installed on the blocks of building, but it is not sufficient to meet the electricity needs of the building. Therefore, a hybrid energy system will be implemented to cover as much of the building's electricity demand as possible. The renewable energy sources used will be solar energy through a photovoltaic system and wind energy through a vertical axis wind turbine (WT). The proposed hybrid system configuration will be implemented in HOMER Pro software which allows a wide analysis along with techno-economic indicators of the different scenarios. Results and comparison are presented to highlight the feasibility of the proposed cases.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Signals Propagation on Tansmission Lines using Analytical Formulae
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper proposes the analysis of the signals propagation on transmission lines using analytical formulae. Where appropriate, the results were compared with those obtained using a well-known circuits simulation program. The study refers to long transmission lines where the reflections are negligible and also to short transmission lines where the signal reflections on the line play a significant role. The main conclusions of the study realized end the paper.

articleTitle: An intelligent wireless monitoring system in telemedicine using IOT technology
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Patient monitoring in healthcare is an important solution to get biometric values. Measurement and display of multiple biometric values such as heart rate, temperature, SpO2, respiration, ECG, etc., is necessary to determine the actual well-being of the patient. This approach is usually implemented in a hospital environment. Population aging and health changes in older patients rises a need for constant monitoring not only in hospital environment but also in every facility where elders live. Monitoring of their activity alongside with biometric values can improve the rate of disease control, lower healthcare costs, faster diagnosis, and lower medical service queue. Wireless Sensor Network (WSNs) play a substantial role in implementing this technology. The proposal in this paper is to create a wireless network of low-cost sensors capable of gathering all the patient physiological data, transmitting this information throw IoT technology for distance monitoring. Creating this approach can help in minimizing the number of social workers in elder facilities but in the same time having a better view of specific disorders in early stages. Using IoT for being able to access the information can help also in analyzing this data, setting some ranges in values we can generate alarms and also start early treatment relying in the data processing.

articleTitle: Computation of Street Lighting in High-Risk Areas. Part II. Curved Roads, Intersections and Roundabouts
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)

articleTitle: Active Power Filter Solution to the Harmonic Issues Caused by a Nonlinear Industrial Load
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper addresses the voltage and current harmonics mitigation issues for a specific large power nonlinear load from automotive industry. Due to the high level of the waveform's distortion and their rapid spectrum change, passive or hybrid filter solutions could not be considered. Accordingly, the usage of an active harmonic filter (AHF) is adopted. The adequate selection of this equipment is conducted after the proper investigation of the main power quality parameters at the industrial load terminals. Consequently, a unit of 300 A rated current was connected in parallel to the load (at low-voltage part of the installation). This manages to constantly reduce the current and voltage harmonics, maintaining their values under the ones prescribed by the actual norms and regulations. The solution is confirmed by the carried-out measurement before and after the active harmonic filter installation.

articleTitle: Enhancing Resilience of Distribution Systems Considering Electric Vehicles and Network Reconfiguration in Post-Extreme Events
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: After extreme events, the uninterrupted power supply to critical loads in the distribution network faces significant challenges. Electric vehicles (EVs), as mobile energy storage units, can supply power to the distribution network through Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology, assisting in the restoration of the distribution network after outages. A collaborative fault restoration strategy is proposed considering the spatiotemporal distribution of EVs supplying power to the distribution network, while also considering the network reconfiguration strategy of the distribution network. The probability of EVs selecting V2G stations and the energy distribution of EVs are characterized. Based on this, a collaborative load restoration strategy considering network reconfiguration of the distribution network is constructed, and the model is formulated as a mixed-integer second-order cone programming (MISOCP) problem. Finally, a case study is conducted using the IEEE 33-node distribution network configuration to verify that the proposed strategy can enhance the load restoration capability in extreme scenarios.

articleTitle: Feasibility of grid-connected residential photovoltaic systems under the new Romanian renewable energy law
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Romania aims to increase the solar share in gross final energy consumption in order to reach the target set until 2030 by the European Union. Thus, the authorities initiated several programs to encourage residential consumers to install grid-connected photovoltaic systems by granting subsidies and improving the regulatory framework for renewable energy. This paper studies the economic feasibility of three photovoltaic systems with different capacities for three residential consumers located in Cluj-Napoca, Romania. The PVSOL Premium 2023 software was employed to simulate the photovoltaic power generation, while Net Present Value and Discounted Payback Period were used to assess the economic feasibility of the systems. The results revealed that the analyzed photovoltaic systems are viable, especially the ones with a higher installed capacity, and cases where residences have a high electricity usage.

articleTitle: Design and Optimisation of a Smart House Lighting System using Arduino
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to create an intelligent lighting system for a prototype house which will be easily accessible for any mobile phone with an Android operating system. On a smaller scale, the authors determined the characteristics of some mini photovoltaic panels, then designed the lighting system for a house model using Arduino and led rings/bands and successfully created a mobile application to control the lighting fixtures. Using this prototype, the students would be able to see the principles of a smart house and could learn how to use photovoltaic panels on a smaller scale. The use of a mobile app is a plus, highlighting the multidisciplinarity of such a project. The main contribution of this paper is creating a prototype which can be used in the learning process through practice for students as a combination of multiple disciplines from the electrical engineering area, thus optimizing the process of information assimilation.

articleTitle: In-wheel Slotless Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor for Light Electric Vehicle Propulsion
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper proposes an in-wheel slotless permanent magnet synchronous motor with toroidal winding for the propulsion of a light electric vehicle. Design evaluation based on 2D finite-element field analysis, proves that the exterior-rotor radial-flux permanent magnet slotless stator with three-phase toroidal winding represents a good-performance choice for light electric traction system.

articleTitle: Helical gears pair optimal design using Genetic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Nowadays environmental concerns and the constant demands of obtaining efficient designs when tackling complex structural problems forced mechanical engineers to use the optimal design methodology. In this paper, a Genetic Algorithm is used to minimize the mass of a helical gear pair mechanism - a key component of an Electric Continuously Variable Transmission - eCVT used as automatic power transmission of various hybrid cars. Designing such mechanisms is an iterative process in which it is necessary to make some tentative choices (for example, the impact of a certain choice of gear width and center distance may yield a minimum mass gearing, but the selection of these values for that parameters may cascade through subsequent steps of the gear design process to ultimately lead to a helical gearing that does not meet the specific strength or manufacturing conditions). The objective function considered here i.e. the mass of the helical gears pairs is computed exactly through a unique method developed by the authors. The optimal design problem is described by a set of 5 design variables (i.e. integer, discrete, and real), and the objective function is subjected to a set o 17 highly non-linear constraints. The results obtained by using GA show significant improvement over the results obtained by traditional design (a 24.21% mass reduction).

articleTitle: The Peculiarities of Steady State Condition of Medium Voltage Cable Line 10 kV in Partial Compensation Mode of Neutral Grounding at Single-phase to Ground Fault
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This work is devoted to the study of the steady state mode of cable line of medium voltage 10 kV at single-phase short circuit with failure current under-compensation at the fault point using an arcing reactor. For the study, a model of a cable line section was elaborated and implemented in the MATLAB-SIMULINK package using available standard elements for modeling the cable line and the supply and additional three-phase transformers. At this the specifics of operation of additional transformer for creation an artificial neutral for connection of arc suppressing reactor was taken into account. A clear picture of the processes occurring in the cable line during under-compensation mode has been obtained, taking into account the real parameters of the cable and transformers. It is shown that in the under-compensation mode, the triangle of linear supply voltages is displaced in a plane-parallel manner so that its vertex connected to the fault point depicts an arc of a circle, which is located in the 1st and 4th quadrants of the complex plane. In this case, the phase currents measured at the beginning of the line (to the left of the fault point) do not depend on the location of the fault. The analysis of symmetrical components of the currents is carried out. It is shown that at a fixed degree of under-compensation with a decreasing of resistance at the fault point this current increase to a certain maximum, determined by the chosen degree of under-compensation and network parameters.

Author Keywords: circle diagrams of cable line voltages and currents

articleTitle: Evaluating the Collective Impact of Nonlinear Residential and Commercial Equipment on Power Quality
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper presents an experimental investigation of harmonic currents produced by sets of nonlinear equipment commonly used in residential and commercial facilities, with different technical specifications. The measurements were conducted with a power quality analyzer, for individual equipment (in isolated operation) as well as for sets of diverse equipment (connected to one socket). Experiments have shown that the combination of compact fluorescent lamps, light emitting diode lamps and personal computers can lead to relatively large cancellation effects of current harmonics, due to the very pronounced diversity effect. When only compact fluorescent lamps and light emitting diode lamps are present, the current harmonics attenuation due to diversity is found to be limited to small effects.

articleTitle: Thermal Behavior of Electrical Contact for Different AC Loads
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The supply of electrical energy to industrial, civil and laboratory equipment and installations takes place by means of contacts and conductors on which a part of the transmitted power is dissipated by thermal effect. Especially on the connection surfaces between the conductors and the loads they feed, such as sockets, contacts, switches, the power dissipated by the thermal effect can have dangerous values. Therefore, the present paper aims to study the data obtained through in-situ measurements in the electrotechnical laboratory on the heating of several types of contacts through which electrical loads are supplied in the laboratory. The measurements were carried out with a high-accuracy thermal imaging camera that determined the thermal behavior of the contacts and conductors at different distances from the connection terminals of the conductor with the electrical loads fed through that conductor. An increase in the temperature of the contacts was found both near the connection. Moreover, this increase depends also on the values of the power absorbed by the load. The change of the temperature of the conductors used in the laboratory was small, not being noticed by the thermal imaging camera. The results of the measurements were then used to develop mathematical models of the dependence of the temperature of the contacts depending on time and depending on the type of load. These models are useful for optimal choice of types of conductors and of different types of connections between the conductors and the load. The measured (real) data and numerical models obtained can also be used in the design of industrial and civil electrical installations.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Determinations for the Internal Resistance of Three Batteries. Three Analytical Methods Involved
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Surprisingly or not, batteries were the primary source of electricity before the development of electric generators and electrical grids. Perhaps Voltaic pile was the first electrical battery that could continuously provide an electric current to a circuit, even if the electrochemical behavior of zinc and copper in a bimetallic arch, in contact with the electrolytes of muscle tissue were observed before. Ordinary batteries consist of one or more electrochemical cells. A cell is created by placing electrodes in an electrolyte where a chemical reaction either generates (at battery use) or uses (at battery recharging) an electric current. Here a very simple circuit has been used to provide raw data for estimating the electromotive force of a power source. The circuit has been used to measure pairs of potential versus intensity for three commercial batteries. From measured data three methods were employed to provide estimates of the internal resistance and electromotive force. The estimating of the internal resistances is discussed.

articleTitle: Electromechanical Conversion Module Design For Flywheel Storage Systems: Requirements Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In this paper is present a short introduction about the flywheel energy storage system and how the system should function for charging or discharging. A method to determine the electromechanical system requirements is also presented, from this method the electrical machine parameters and mechanical characteristic can be determined.

articleTitle: House heating system thermal dynamics assessment using Petri Net approach
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Energy efficiency is important as a way towards achieving energy savings and lowering harmful greenhouse gas emissions, and it also opens opportunities for employment and growth for new areas of activity boosting investment. Residential buildings have an important share in the energy used for different activities. As most of the energy used in residential buildings is aimed for space heating, the heating system must be assessed in terms of energy efficiency related to low heat losses. The paper proposed a Petri Net approach for modelling and simulating the dynamics of thermal heating system of a house in order to reduce the energy consumption based on appropriated heating system behavior.

articleTitle: Research on Identifying Parallel Resonance in Power Networks using Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The distribution power systems often supply consumers that contain nonlinear loads; so, the power system operates under a stationary harmonic distorted regime. On the other hand, these consumers have resistive-inductive components that cause the circulation of reactive power and consequently need to use VAr compensation. The interaction between these phenomena can cause parallel resonance events. The research presented in this article had the goal to determine the feasibility of using artificial neural networks to identify parallel resonance in harmonic polluted power systems, more specifically at the consumer's side. The first step in this research was to obtain the necessary data to train, test and validate the proposed methodology. For this, a MATLAB / Simulink model was used. The next step involved the evaluation of the data to determine the correspondence to the parallel resonance events. The research's last step entailed the training and testing of an artificial neuronal network. The results showed that the use of this method is successful in predicting and identifying parallel resonance phenomena in harmonically polluted networks.

articleTitle: Numerical simulations for a direct drive horizontal axis micro-wind turbine
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper presents some simulation results of a small power wind turbine. This study is divided in two parts: first, the aerodynamic simulations are targeting the development of a high efficiency with low cut-in speed blade and second, the identification of the most efficient and cost-effective direct drive permanent magnet generator. The results are highlighting the recommended blade torsion angle and the most cost-effective permanent magnet generator.

Author Keywords: spoke type outer rotor permanent magnet generator

articleTitle: Loop Closing of Flyback Switching Power Supply Using Inductive Coupling. Practical Study
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The main purpose of this paper is the practical study of closing the reaction loop of sources in flyback switching using inductive coupling. The advantage of this source is that one does not need to use an optocoupler to pass the signals from the secondary to the primary and therefore the variation range of the output voltage with temperature is reduced. In this sense, the following stages are completed: the simulation of the wireless transfer module of electromagnetic energy, followed by the practical realization of this module; carrying out laboratory experiments using power supplies in flyback switching, with the closing of the reaction loop through the main transformer, using inductive coupling. The magnetic circuits used to build the power supply are also analyzed by simulation.

articleTitle: Non-Linear Smooth PWM Control of Power Electronic Installation with Two Stator Windings of Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This publication presents the results of a study of two-inverter electric drive with two stator windings of an electric motor, regulated on the basis of modified algorithms of synchronous pulsewidth modulation (PWM), which provide a nonlinear relationship between the voltage on the motor windings and the frequency of the system (<tex>$V/F$</tex>) in the process of regulation. Therefore, such nonlinear <tex>$V/F$</tex> control dependences can provide effective operation of ac drives with some specific control regimes and loads. Thus, the modified algorithms of feedforward multi-zone PWM provide synchronization and symmetries of the base voltages for any control modes of operation of systems including modes with a fractional ratio between the switching frequency of inverters and fundamental frequency of system. Behavior of systems with some typical linear and non-linear <tex>$V/F$</tex> control modes is analyzed and simulated.

articleTitle: Designing a FPGA- based implementation of hardware-software instrument for in-site solar panels evaluation
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The current research paper is focused on designing and hardware-software tool for fast evaluation of an industrial solar panel in local working conditions. It is based on a standard PV model, and by using an IGBT- based controlled load, the hardware-software evaluates the PV response in real time conditions. Tests has been conducted in irradiation and temperature dependencies, then a shadow influence has been introduced into the model and the results have been compared with the measured data. The shapes and the ranges of the obtained data allowed us to build a procedure for in-site tests for running PV systems.

articleTitle: Adapting the Impedance of The Signal Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Impedance matching is a practical procedure used to design the input impedance of an electrical load or the output impedance of the signal source, for power transfer maximization or for minimizing the reflection of the signal from the load. Starting from the correct definition of impedance matching in electrical engineering, the paper aims to present the necessary steps for the design and construction of impedance matching. Therefore, a rigorous calculation is required, through several procedures, of the values of the associated parameters. To achieve the above-mentioned objectives, the work goes through the following stages: defining the adaptation of the purely resistive impedance using a line of length λ/4, followed by the calculation of the impedance value of the adaptation line; adaptation of a complex load using passive elements with lumped parameters (coils or capacitors) with presentation of adaptation using two purely reactive components; practical examples of adapting a complex load to a line section using a series-parallel circuit, conclusions and bibliography.

articleTitle: Project-oriented approach in teaching programming to the first year undergraduate students in Electrical Engineering
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper presents the approach of teaching and learning programing languages within the Computer Programming and Programming Languages course taught to the 1<sup>st</sup> year of study undergraduate students from the Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Technical University of Cluj Napoca, based on solving simple Electrical Engineering problems. This approach was extended recently within an Erasmus Blended Intensive Program, through the project entitled DIG-SENSING. The students learn the basic of C/C++ programming through exercises that involve mathematics, physics, theory of electric circuits and other disciplines while they have the opportunity to understand better the use of programming languages in designing engineering applications by hands on experiments exercises and projects. The practical classes include solving problems using the programming languages C, C++, C# and Python. This paper presents laboratory practical examples and projects introduced to increase the student's interest and motivation in learning programming in the context of solving engineering problems. The paper also describes the course related activities such as webinars and presentations of using programming languages in realizing Electrical Engineering practical applications and an evaluation of students perception on learning programming through project oriented approach.

articleTitle: A method for extracting the main parameters of a NPN bipolar transistor from datasheet for use in the SPICE model
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In this paper, starting from a model already existing in the SPICE library of a NPN bipolar transistor, the parameters of this model are verified, and some models are proposed for extracting these parameters from the datasheet. The validation of these parameters is done in SPICE simulations comparing the results with the information from the datasheet. The following parameters of the NPN bipolar transistor are validated: amplification factor, transition factor, emitter resistance, base resistance, collector resistance, IRB, BF, BR, IKS, IS, ISE, VAF, CJE, CJC.

articleTitle: A Wideband Patch Antenna with Symmetrical Notches at 3.5 GHz: Design and Achievement
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: A compact patch antenna with a notched contour is proposed, analyzed, fabricated and used for receiving 5G mobile communication signals in the FR1 range. The bandwidth at a voltage standing ware ratio <tex>$(\text{VSWR}) < 1.5$</tex> is 340 MHz, the resonance frequency is 3.55 GHz and its total efficiency is higher than 73% over the whole band. The maximum gain in the band is 3.42 dBi, while the antenna is slightly directive with the main beam as large as 87.1 degrees. The measured versus simulated VSWR is not significantly different. With these characteristics the antenna is mitigating interference from other unwanted signals in the 5G band, especially when time division duplexing system is in use. After its fabrication, the antenna's versatility is checked in a receiving situation nearby a targeted mobile phone in real life usage conditions. It is demonstrated that its response conforms the initial established requirements.

articleTitle: Low Cost High Precision Multiple Purposes Automatic Syringe
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The laboratories use automatic syringes to reduce the work volume and increase the precision of their measurements. The solutions available on the market are very expensive. In this paper, we propose the development of a new 3D printed automatic syringe that can be used by students to complete the titration experiments. This product is precise, modular and it can be used remotely, so the students won't need to be on site for their studies. The cost of such a device compared to the existing ones on the market is much smaller, but it has similar performances.

articleTitle: Evaluation of an Electrical Modified Surgical Circular Stapler: A testing and validation study
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The digitalization of medical devices has revolutionized the field of surgery, enhancing precision, efficiency, and patient outcomes. This paper explores the application of digitalization in the context of mechanical surgical staplers, specifically focusing on circular staplers (CSs). The objective of this study is to validate an electronic system built to measure the pressure dynamics at the tip of circular staplers during surgical procedures. Testing will be conducted on anesthetized pigs, allowing for real-time observation and analysis. The findings from this research will contribute to the understanding of how digitalization can optimize the use of circular staplers in real-life surgical interventions.

articleTitle: Optimization of the connection conditions of a 2.4 MW Photovoltaic Power Plant on a quasi-charged medium voltage distributor
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: As the implementation of MW order photovoltaic power plants (PV) gathers a significant number of specialists, their connection to the medium voltage (MV) distributors involves problems related to the following aspects: determining the place and point of connection (distance from the electrical station busbars), the degree of the distributor charge in the context of the entire network related to the respective station, maintaining the voltage level within the range provided by the grid operator, the analysis of the PV connection in the extreme scenarios, related to the real load in the considered scheme, the voltage level to which the PV is connected. The above aspects have been considered and dealt with in this article for the purpose of connecting a 2.4 MW PV to an MV distributor with a high degree of charge due to the existing power plants or those with technical approval obtained for connection. Thus, after modeling the MV network and running the steady-state calculation program, its characteristic values have been checked if they are within the allowed value ranges in accordance with the performance standard. After determining the situation generated by coupling the PV to the grid and highlighting the negative aspects, several methods for optimizing the integration of the power injection point into the grid were proposed.

articleTitle: Radiofrequency Electromagnetic Field Level Inside and Outside Measurements in a Building: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Nowadays radio frequency electromagnetic field exposure in urban environment is an important topic due to a large number of electromagnetic waves emitted by antennas that vary in intensity throughout the day. The main objective of this research was to establish if the exposure level of electromagnetic field from different areas (three sites specifically) was within the ICNIRP (International Commission on Non-Ionizing Radiation Protection) limits. The measurement method used was frequency selective on 420 MHz - 3 GHz frequency range. The results demonstrated that the surface power density ranges from 0.04 mW/m2 to 0.24 mW/m2, with a maximum value of 0.30 V/m for the total electric field and a minimum value of 0.12 V/m. The highest measured values were obtained on building roof top location, which were attributed to the large number of antennas present at the site. The report concluded that, the results are below those indicated by international standards.

articleTitle: Digital Electronics for Everyone: Custom Hands-on Experience for Students - Multiplexing and Demultiplexing with the help of an Open-Hardware Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper presents an alternative teaching platform build around an open-source hardware, for studying digital electronics applications. The aim of the proposed system is to facilitate the examination of digital multiplexing circuits, while providing a flexible approach in designing custom applications. Furthermore, the hands-on experience is enhanced through various input configurations and hardware-emulated logical functions.

articleTitle: Battery Balancing System for Electric Vehicles Solar Power Assisted
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Battery system is a simple and widely used electrical energy storage system for industry, UPS, intelligent applications, vehicles, electrical appliances and others. It can drive the integration of the vehicle and the power grid. In high power applications, the battery is joint in series to enhance the potential and joint in parallel to increase the current, but because of the processing conditions of the battery and the imbalance between each cell, the total power is reduced. One of the most common balancing methods used today is passive balancing, which is based on the principle that a power resistor incorporated in series discharges the excess when one of the cells reaches the voltage or charge threshold so that the other cells can be charged. The present project intends to propose a solar power to balance the battery of an electric vehicle. There are three approaches of process: the first is solar balancing, which uses solar energy to charge the accumulator according to the lowest state of charge (SOC) while driving, the second refers to the energy stored in the memory cell which is delivered via the DC-DC converter to the accumulator cell with the lowest SOC, and the third is charging according to the altitude SOC when the vehicle is charging from an outlet and is parked. For the simulation, it has been used a battery pack with four 13.8 V Etch One, batteries connected in series. Conformable to the results of simulation, the proposed method can economize 1.465% to 1.904% of a 50 Ah battery pack total capacity every 13.2 km. The accumulator pack can be balanced when the solar current is about 6–7 A. The balancing remains very successful even if the solar current is reduced to 2–3 A or if the cell storage mode is used with the identical current limitation.

articleTitle: Assessment of Electromagnetic Interferences Produced by a Photovoltaic On-Grid System
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The main source of electromagnetic interference in the case of photovoltaic systems are the DC-DC and DC-AC converters which are based on high frequency electronic switching devices. The electromagnetic interferences are transferred both inside the Photovoltaic (PV) system and outside, On-Grid. Due to the frequent use of photovoltaic systems in residential and industrial applications, the resulting interferences shall be known and controlled. There are several regulations to prevent the transmission of interference, but the development of efficient EMI filters is still a challenge. The purpose of this paper is to assess the electromagnetic interferences produced by photovoltaic on-grid system by measurements. Conducted and harmonic current emissions are analyzed according to SR EN 55014-1:2017 and SR EN IEC 61000-3-2:2019 standards, respectively. A home residence PV system with five Eurener panel (450W each) string, a SUN2000- 2/3/3.68/4/4.6/5/6KTL-L1 2kW inverter, for several loads is analyzed.

articleTitle: Position Control Application with Simatic S7-1500T and Sinamics S210
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Position control with PLC represents one of the high complexity software applications in the field of industrial automation. In this paper the authors present an automation design of two-axis control using Sinamics S210 and S7-1511T PLC which are useful for electrical engineering master's students. To provide an experience closer to real world applications and one that should allow the study of PLC programming, the PROFINET industrial communication protocol, design screens for Human Machine Interfaces (HMI) and positioning applications, the students can use the proposed solution in the faculty laboratories. They can start with the development of elementary complexity software applications, all the way to high complexity applications.

articleTitle: Industrial Communication Networks Used within SAW Sensors Data Transmission
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper presented some comparative aspects of industrial communication networks used in substations regarding temperature monitoring of electrical equipment by sound acoustic wave SAW sensors. The current communication methods found within the electrical equipment are presented. On last part of the paper, are highlight the advantages and disadvantages of the current communication methods used within SAW Sensors Data Transmission. The communication networks are various and suitable for particular cases. In the paper, it was argued the choice of a certain type of communication was used for SAW sensors temperature monitoring of electrical equipment.

articleTitle: Validation of PV numerical simulation model with an experimental setup
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The renewable energy industry has experienced continuous growth, as humanity looks for more sustainable ways to produce electrical energy. Today, photovoltaics represents the biggest share of the renewable energy industry The study begins with a presentation of the working principles of a photovoltaic panel. Then a numerical model of a photovoltaic panel is developed, based on actual characteristics from a commercial panel. The main goal is to produce a model capable of analyzing the different operating conditions of solar panels and predict their behavior by employing the appropriate parameters. The model is built in Matlab/ SIMULINK, based on the equivalent circuit of PV cells. The results are validated with experimental test data obtained by operating the PV panel both with an indoor solar simulator and the real sun. In both cases the modelled and experimental results are very close.

articleTitle: Study of a Residual Current Device behavior for half-waves and break times corelated with the phase angle of tripping currents
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to study and observe the behavior of Residual Current Device (RCD) in relation with starting angle variances of the tripping current. Many experiments are carried out by measuring tripping current and type of devices of different typology, produced by different manufacturers. In order to determine the behavior of RCD to the different starting angle of the tripping current comparative analysis were carried out between the real model of the device and the mathematical simulation of the equivalent electrical parameters of the device. The main objective is to identify which parameter of the electrical model has the biggest influence on the behavior of RCD in relation with the starting phase angle of the tripping current.

articleTitle: Evaluating ML Algorithm precision over indoor thermal comfort through comparison of popular metrics
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Predicting the temperature in indoor spaces is essential for upholding cozy living and working conditions as well as for assuring the security and preservation of delicate tools and materials. This parameter's forecast beforehand can aid in reducing hazards, enhancing operations, and improving energy efficiency. In this paper, data retrieved from sensors, positioned within a particular building, has been simulated through three machine learning ML models. Machine Learnings (ML) become a potent tool for temperature prediction based on historical data, weather patterns, and other related elements in recent years. We evaluated the performance of three machine learning (ML) models using a train and test dataset. This paper focuses on identifying the best model selection comparing the three chosen models.

articleTitle: Study of EMI Stress on DC-to-DC converter based on Software Simulations
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: From the first electronic control unit (ECU) in the car (e.g., radio 50 years ago) to more than 80 ECUs in the car nowadays (e.g.., vehicle-to-vehicle communication - V2V, vehicle-to-environment communication - V2I, vehicle-to-everything communication - V2X and ultra-high-speed-mobile-low-latency internet) the electromagnetic interference (EMI) problems increased dramatically. In a modern self-driving car, the EMI stress is a safety critical issue. A good design of an ECU must also provide a robust concept of all safety applications in a harsh EMI environment but not only the comfort. This paper shows different developing directions of an EMI robust ECU. For better understanding, an example for studying the EMI stress on a dc-dc converter used in automotive LED light application is carried out by numerical simulations to check the robustness of the electronic system under study by compliance with the EMC requirement of the customers or the standards. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Improving security in the operation of nuclear power plants using Defence in Depth principle
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper presents a study on the impact of using Defence-in-Depth principle to improve security in operation of the nuclear power plants. The simulation results showed that the use of characteristics to ensure the layers of Defence in Depth, such as redundancy, in the design of the Auxiliary Power Supply System, increased the reliability of the system by up to 26.7%. The results suggest that the Defence in Depth principle is effective in improving the security and reliability of power plant systems and equipment. This study provides a framework for future evaluations of other Defence in Depth characteristics on the reliability of power plants systems and equipment.

articleTitle: Comprehensive temperature characterization of a thermal system using distributed RC networks
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The aim of this study was to develop a method for determining the thermal behavior of any thermal system by identifying thermal parameters for multidisciplinary behavioral models. The proposed solution refines the minimum structure of the thermoelectric model using an iterative least squares method and the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm, and a graph of the spectral density of time constants. This approach reduces the influence of the filtering factor during the deconvolution operation, enabling the construction of a thermal model using the structural function of the thermal characteristic transition. These findings have potential implications for the development of integrated circuit behavioral models that account for thermal processes.

articleTitle: A Multi-Agent Approach for Solving the Power Distribution State Estimation in the Context of micro-PMUs
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The integration of a considerable number of small distributed generation units has already started to disturb the design, construction and operation of power distributed networks. In such conditions, for the distribution system to withstand and accomplish the Power Quality (PQ) standard requirements, a rapid and coordinated control is crucial to be performed. For the control system to accomplish its objective, the power distribution system state has to be determined rapidly. The direct measurement and time synchronized of the complex voltage is done using the technology of micro-PMUs. The decreased cost for the acquisition and installation of micro-PMU, has made it a viable tool for providing data to the real time. Classically, when the number of PMUs ensure the network observability, the state estimation is computed by using a procedure named linear state estimation. In this paper, the technology of multi-agent system (MAS) is investigated for solving the state estimation problem. It was implemented in Matlab a power flow module who simulates measurements by adding stochastic errors. The complex values of voltage and currents are the send to the MAS for computing the state estimation. In order to evaluate the performances of the proposed MAS algorithm, a classic linear state estimation was implemented in parallel and the 2 solutions were then compared, both for each PMU in part, and also at a global level.

articleTitle: Design Solutions for Reducing AC resistance of High Frequency Windings
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Electromagnetic devices operating at high frequencies (hundreds of kHz) are becoming increasingly present in applications that regards switching and data transmission. In this sense, their windings are increasingly made of Litz type wires in several configurations. The present paper reveals a comparative FEMM study between the most used configurations. The numerical analysis of the skin and proximity effect influence at frequencies up to 500 kHz was pursued. The Litz#7 configuration proves to have the best performance. Afterwards, a comparative study is carried out between the values of alternating current resistance values, determined numerically and those analytically calculated with formulas known from the specialized literature.

articleTitle: An Application of LIDAR Technology for Wind Speed Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The ongoing growth of electricity consumption, along with decarbonization policies adopted worldwide, implies a steeper rate regarding the use of such renewable and clean energy sources. The proper evaluation of wind potential is of utmost importance for developing a wind farm project, as it allows the identification of the optimum site for wind turbine installation and the type of wind turbine to be installed in that specific site. This paper aims to evaluate the wind potential in a particular site from the north side of Romania's Moldova region, measuring the wind speeds at various altitudes using the cutting-edge technology of Laser Imaging, Detection, and Ranging (LIDAR). Measurements were conducted at multiple heights, over an entire year, with data being processed and analyzed. The wind speed was evaluated, along with the duration for each recorded speed, and wind direction. Thus, the wind potential in the considered area was evaluated.

articleTitle: Automation and integration in SCADA system of the wastewater treatment plant in Cantemir, Moldova
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In this paper, the problem was the realization of a SCADA system (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) and an automation system for the system of the wastewater treatment plant in Cantemir, Moldova. The use of innovative treatment methods based on revolutionary industrial principles, such as Imhoff, reduces maintenance costs, increases energy efficiency and contributes to improving the quality of the water that is fed by the people who live in this city. Following the implementation of the SCADA automated system, water remains free of microorganisms, parasites or substances that, by number or concentration, constitute a potential danger to human health, and energy efficiency in an automation system is an important point that is analyzed and implemented in each electromechanical system separately, to reduce system maintenance costs and increase flexibility.

articleTitle: Adaptive HF radio channels based on signal-to-noise ratio using SDR technology
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Adaptive HF (high-frequency) radio channels based on signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) using software-defined radio (SDR) technology is a promising approach to improve the reliability and efficiency of radio communications. The HF radio communication channel is often affected by channel fading, which degrades the signal-to-noise ratio of the received signal. Adaptive techniques can be used to adjust the transmission parameters based on the channel conditions, such as SNR, to mitigate the effects of channel degradation and improve the reliability of HF radio communications. In the paper, we discuss the need for adaptive RF radio channels, the advantages of SDR technology and Python programming combined with the GNU Radio block library. We also propose a specific method for adaptive HF radio channels based on SNR and evaluate this method in the laboratory.

articleTitle: Simulation and Analysis of Electrical Loads used for Automotive Electrical Circuits
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In order to test various equipment that operate based on electronic power converters, in most cases, it is necessary to use an energy-consuming circuit with a variable - controlled consumption regime. The purpose of this paper is to highlight parametric or programmable electrical loads using electronic devices.

articleTitle: A New Method and Device of Voltage Normalization in Electric Grids
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The research is aimed at developing effective solutions for solving problems with deviation of power grid parameters. One of the important technological tasks in this case is the regulation of the voltage. To solve the problem, it is proposed to use patented devices of Demand Side Management - AC voltage normalizers NORMEL<sup>™®©</sup>. Previous papers present in detail the results of scientific research and long-term practical experience in the use of AC voltage normalizers in electrical networks with a voltage level of 0.4 kV. This paper presents a new patented schematic diagram of the AC voltage normalizer operation that allows you to increase the power of devices.

articleTitle: Temperature Monitoring of MV Switchgear Cabinet by Non-Intrusive Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper aims to presents a review about the wireless monitoring methods used to identify the thermal stresses of electrical equipment within Medium Voltage (MV) switchgear cabinet. There are presented several advantages and disadvantages of the current non-intrusive methods of the electrical equipment temperature monitoring. In the final part of the paper there are presented the results obtained from a laboratory experiment, which aimed to highlight the disadvantages of the sound acoustic waves (SAW) monitoring of a busbar. Also, in the case study it intend to present in what matter the SAW monitoring method is appropriate for MV Switchgear Cabinet.

articleTitle: Rotary DBD Plasma Reactor for Inline Treatment of Polymeric Substrates
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to present the effects of DBD non-thermal plasma treatment on the surfaces of polymeric foils used in packaging industry, namely <tex>$20\ \mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> thickness PET foil. The treatment was performed in air, at atmospheric pression and humidity, using a rotary DBD discharge. The reactor was design to allow inline treatment of the substrate in roll-to-roll configuration. The plasma was generated using a high voltage and high frequency power supply. Two different voltage values of 8.5 and 7 kV were considered while the frequency was in the range of 16.6 kHz. The effects of the plasma treatment were evaluated by measuring the water contact angle (WCA) using a goniometer and the surface tension using Arcotest test pens. The influence of discharge voltage, treatment time and foil speed were evaluated. The results indicated a decrease of PET surface WCA from over 75 to around 30 degrees after DBD treatment, even for treatment times of 65 ms, while the surface tension is increasing from 36 mN/m to over 60 mN/m.

articleTitle: Aspects Regarding the Influence of the Supply Voltage on the Torque, Respectively the Efficiency of a Brushless DC Motor with Variable Geometry
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper aims to study the influence of the power supply voltage of a brushless DC (BLDC) motor with variable geometry on the torque and its efficiency parameters in two extreme geometric instances, called Geom. 0 - unformed and Geom. 10 - total deformed. The motor rotor has a variable geometry due to the specific design of permanent magnets called compound magnets which are elastic. The BLDC motor is started from 0 rpm and no resistant load (torque) up to the rated speed of rotation when the resistant load is applied. The stator and rotor geometries are modeled only to be able to extract some data from the FEM simulations and are not optimized according to all the design rules and principles of BLDC electric machines, since the purpose of the present study is the comparison of the machine behaviors at different geometric instances of the rotor.

articleTitle: Development and Optimization of a Broadside-Coupled Dual-Band Microstrip Bandpass Filter for Wireless Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In this article, we present the development and optimization of a dual-band microstrip bandpass filter for frequencies between 2.47 - 2.68 GHz and 5.04-5.29 GHz. Starting with a brief introduction to the field of filtering and wireless communication, we explore numerical modeling using ANSYS HFSS software, followed by practical implementation and measurement of the filter parameters. We detail how changes in geometry, dielectric, and coupling can influence filter performance, and present results by comparing simulated data with experimental results. This article will be useful for engineers and researchers looking to understand and develop efficient filters for wireless applications.

articleTitle: Electrical Grounding Design of a Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper presents an overview of grounding design of wind turbines based on two mainframes: the power frequency grounding resistances and the impulse grounding resistances. Considering every possible way, depending on the variables that are implied in the design process, the grounding resistances are calculated, also the touch voltage and contact voltage has been considered and compared to the standard limit. The paper shows the feasibility of impulse grounding resistances of the adapted design, having different soil resistivity and is compared to the withstand value of safety measure and confirmation of the personal safety is acquired.

articleTitle: Smart Grid LAB Hessen – Investigation of the development of the low-voltage grid to challenging grid situations in 2020, 2030 and 2045
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In the previous article “Smart Grid LAB Hessen - a real-life test environment for active distribution grids” the project “Smart Grid LAB Hessen” and its rough structure were explained. Scenarios for the development and penetration of renewable energy technologies for the years 2020, 2030 and 2045 were developed, which can be derived from the goals of the German Federal Government. Furthermore, the scenario “full expansion” of the prosumer was created. This article describes all four scenarios and the insights gained from them. This is followed by an outlook on how the laboratory will proceed.

articleTitle: The process of development of railway vehicle subsistems
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The article presents the development process of railway vehicle subsystems in the context of meeting the safety requirements of the specific standards. Railway subsystems must be qualified to meet the required safety conditions so that operation is safe for the persons and does not adversely affect the environment or other goods. The multitude of applicable regulations requires the existence of a process to guide designers. By applying this it is possible to obtain subsystems that meet the conditions of reliability, availability, maintainability and safety and in this way can be qualified as usable in the railway field.

articleTitle: Availability and Reliability Evaluation of Romanian hydro generating units using Markov analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper uses a Markov reliability model for two hydro power plants using the operational data for a twelve years span (2010 ÷2021). The availability and reliability of individual generating units and for the power plant are evaluated taking into account different case studies using failure rate λ, repair rate μ, MTTR, MTBF, MTTF, state probability, frequency of state and rate of departure.

articleTitle: Influence of Various Defects on Power Cable Insulation Under AC Electric Field
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In this study, we present 3D numerical models for analyzing the impact of various defects, including cavities, vented and bow-tie water trees, on the insulation of a 20 kV power cable under an AC voltage of 50 Hz. Specifically, we examine the effects of vented tree lengths on the AC electric field in the polymer region that is free of defects, in a cavity located in front of the tree, and in a bow-tie tree growing towards the vented tree. Additionally, we discuss the implications of these defects on the power losses in the polymeric insulation of the cable.

articleTitle: Acquisition and Monitoring System for Basic Laboratory Measurements on Electrical Networks Parameters
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to present a solution for basic measurements of the electrical networks parameters. The classical measurement procedure, using analog measurement devices, is replaced with a simple modular data acquisition system, based on a signal conditioning module with Hall Effect transducers. Due to the simplicity of the sensorial acquisition module, it is easy to use for single or multiple phase electrical networks. With the aid of a data acquisition board, the signals were transferred to a virtual instrument, which can compute and display specific quantities that are commonly used in electrical networks monitoring and control processes. The circuits presented in this paper were included in laboratory classes like: Electrical Measurements, Instrumentation and Data Acquisitions, Legal and Applied Metrology. Comparative measurements were performed, comparing the results from three different sources: analog devices, oscilloscope, and data acquisition system. Considering the fact that the presented solution is a didactic one, the user interface has an important role, where the students can simulate various practical situations and compare them with the real measured ones.

articleTitle: Equivalent Models of Nonlinear Circuit Elements in Nonsinusoidal Regime
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The circuits containing voltage or charge controlled nonlinear capacitors (qc), or current or flux controlled nonlinear inductors (cc), or current or voltage controlled nonlinear resistors can be simulated using the dedicated software SPICE by developing equivalent models for these circuit elements. Using macro-models, with equivalent schemes which model the voltage or current sources controlled by the time derivatives of the voltage and current respectively, this paper described all types of nonlinear circuit elements, in SPICE, with the corresponding sub-circuits. These sub-circuits allow the simulation of these circuits in time domain, using either SPICE or Symbolic State Equation Generation (SYSEG) programs. Then, by using the FFT function form MATLAB's toolbox, the circuits were analyzed in frequency domain, to underline the currents, the voltages and the harmonic spectrum which present interest.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electromagnetic Radiation on a Seagoing Vessel
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper represents a study on electromagnetic radiations starting from their generation, the disturbances they produce in the operation of the electro-energetic equipment on board of a maritime vessel as well as the analysis of the aspects related to the effect on the health of the crew. Measurements have been carried out on a seagoing vessel. The values obtained from measuring the electromagnetic field radiations have been analysed. The values obtained for the purpose of taking protective measures for the electro-energetic equipment and crew are presented.

articleTitle: Practical implementation for efficiency evaluation of hydrogen production methods
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to build a test stand for a hydrogen generator and analyze the working principle regarding different operation parameters in normal temperature and pressure conditions. Hydrogen is one of the most abundant elements in the entire Universe. Even though hydrogen is a colorless tasteless and odorless gas, in the literature it is given a series of colors that underline the method of the gas production or extraction. For example, green hydrogen is made using renewable energy and using electrolysis, purple hydrogen is made using nuclear power and heat and there are more colors regarding the production method and the impact it has on the environment. Hydrogen production is just a process of splitting water into the 2 components, hydrogen and oxygen and using hydrogen means merging those two gases back together. Splitting them requires energy and merging them back generates energy so in other words hydrogen is an energy vector. The main challenge is the way hydrogen is generated, stored, transported, and used. All those processes that involve hydrogen must be feasible from an economic point of view. For the storage problem there are already some solutions implemented in different areas with different storage and further use solutions.

articleTitle: The Design and Applications of Dashboards Used in Electrical and Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: There are numerous ways of displaying data to be analyzed and interpreted professionally, but few are well-shaped with the process, the key indicators, and the needs of the users. In this paper, the following will be presented: the different ways in which data can be visualized, the main elements which constitute a modern dashboard, the impact of data visualization on the users of the dashboard, and the decision-making process. A dashboard can be described as a tool that incorporates different indicators used by its designated users to aid them in the process of taking appropriate actions toward the achievement of the performance goals of a company. It is a tool that measures performance but can also predict imminent risks and impact the safety levels of the company workers and assets. The following are some of the main characteristics that are going to be presented in this paper: including key process indicators, callings attention to important results and findings, using a data representation model based on the grouping of different relevant indicators, guiding the user to be user-friendly and intuitive, creating different visualization models (for example graphs, pie charts, and icons) to help the user understand the data presented. The most favorable role of a dashboard is to impact its user decision-making action positively. The design, placement, and functionality of the different elements of a dashboard, for example, the graphs, icons, and indicators, must be carefully considered and planned. In this paper, each element that comprises a dashboard, and the different ways of creating it will be surveyed. In the final chapter, a compelling design philosophy for creating such a tool will be summarized.

articleTitle: Synchronous Power Transfer to Induction Motors Operating with Variable Frequency Drives Case 2: Supervised Fast Transfer
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The supervised synchronous transfer of an induction motor between a variable frequency drive (VFD) output and the main supply represents a precise procedure aiming to eliminate the drawbacks represented by hard transients. The paper analyses the process of fast synchronous transfer and highlights the advantages over the unsupervised fixed time synchronization. Preliminary tests lead to the implementation of a functional control systems which proven to be useful in confirming the overall superiority of the fast transfer method. A Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) assures the supervision of the fast transfer process. Specific captured waveforms of the system operating at specific times reveal as safe transfer of the induction motor between the two sources, accompanied by a smooth and short transient regime.

articleTitle: Monitoring the Parameters Obtained by Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The increase of energy demand has made PV modules more affordable for energy consumers. Years of research and monitoring the parameters of PV systems has made the continuous development and improvement of photovoltaic systems possible. This article focuses on the monitoring of parameters obtained by photovoltaic systems installed at several residential buildings.

articleTitle: Matlab Simulink Simulation of Faults and Abnormal Operating Regimes in a Medium Voltage Network with Isolated Neutral for the Purpose of Coordinating Protection Settings
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: An important role in ensuring the continuous supply of electricity to consumers is determined by protection installations. Solving their selectivity and sensitivity leads to lower demands on the primary equipment, reducing the times to eliminate abnormal operating regimes and faults in the network, as well as obtaining better network-related power quality indicators. Therefore, both the choice of the most appropriate protection functions and the coordination of their settings is an aspect to which we must pay special attention. In the present work, a 20 kV network with isolated neutral was modeled, by means of the MatLab Simulink simulation software, and simulations were done corresponding to several faults and abnormal operating regimes. Following the analysis of the obtained results, the most appropriate protection functions were chosen and very well coordinated settings were proposed to ensure the selectivity and sensitivity of the protections.

articleTitle: High Power Inductive Coupler Design From a Downscaled Model
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Wireless power transfer systems are considered by many experts, possible solutions for smart charging of the batteries of future non-pollutant heavy duty electric vehicles, such as electric buses, electric trucks etc. The development of wireless power transfer system prototypes for heavy duty electric vehicles that are inherently characterized by high rated powers (hundreds of kW) is very expensive and their optimizations would entail huge costs. This paper analyzes the possibility of dimensioning a high-power inductive coupler for heavy electric vehicles based on a ~kW downscaled model so that a preliminary study can be carried out at acceptable price levels. The following main parameters were considered for the dimensional scaling: the distance between transmitter and receiver coils, the magnetic coupling factor, the operation frequency, the coupler area and the transmitted power. Keeping the same coupling factor for the real and downscaled models is a basic condition that is followed in this study for a transmitted power density at a given power ratio.

articleTitle: The Importance of Switching to Green Energy from Photovoltaic Sources and its Impact on the Industrial Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
