abstract: The topic of the article is associated with the current concern, at a global level, in the sector of energy from renewable sources, with an emphasis on the conversion of photovoltaic energy into electricity. This paper mainly promotes the advantages of switching to the use of alternative energy sources in the supply of electricity for industrial spaces such as: production halls, storage halls, agricultural halls, etc. This article highlights the important environmental factors that greatly influence the performance of a photovoltaic system, namely the location, the amount of absorbed sunlight-which is essential in any photovoltaic system for its financial feasibility, solar irradiation, solar insulation, electricity production depending on available solar hours per day, air mass, Sun angle, PV orientation and shading level. Also, in this paper it is made a review of the important electrical characteristics for photovoltaic cells such as maximum output power, short circuit current, open circuit voltage, filling factor, power produced by solar cells, solar intensity and the negative way in which the temperature at a very high level decreases the performance of the photovoltaic cells. The purpose of the study is to focus on what must be taken into account at a theoretical level and not only for the implementation of such a system with a good efficiency on the spaces that serve the industrial environment, following the possibilities of expanding the use of green energy and reducing the CO<inf>2</inf> footprint and greenhouse gases.

articleTitle: Study on Specific Tests for Low-Voltage Electrical Equipment
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Low Voltage (LV) electrical equipment and appliances, those that operate powered at voltages ranging from 0 to 1000V [1], are most common in both households, IT and industrial applications. In this paper, experimental tests measuring electrical power and current and insulation resistance for two types of irons and the heating study for an IT equipment are presented. The experimental results were analysed by specific calculations on the determination of measurement uncertainties and compared with the values specified in international standards. The experimental determinations were carried out in the Low Voltage Laboratory of the National Research, Development and Testing Institute for Electrical Engineering - ICMET Craiova, a RENAR accredited laboratory.

articleTitle: Energy efficiency first, from a slogan to a reality with impact in the urban environment
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The authors discuss the importance of energy efficiency, starting from the concept of “Energy Efficiency first” to its actual realisation as a tool to improve the quality of life and energy services and to make energy prices more affordable, especially still in the context of the energy crisis.

articleTitle: Single-Stage NPC-Type Dual-Port Inverter for Integrated Wind/Battery Hybrid System
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Wind power is inherently intermittent and poses challenges to the stable integration of wind turbines (WTs) into a power system. Battery energy storage systems (BESSs) are often used to mitigate wind power fluctuations, charging and discharging batteries depending on wind conditions. Like every multisource system, the WT-BESS hybrid system requires power electronic converters to control the dc and ac power flows. Multiple dc-dc and dc-ac power conversion stages enable high control flexibility, but have a low energy conversion efficiency and require several bulky passive filters. Single-stage multiport inverters (MPIs) that connect multiple sources to the ac grid in a single conversion stage have been increasingly investigated in recent years as a potential alternative. This paper examines the performance of the NPC-type Dual-Port Inverter (DPI) for a wind energy system based on a permanent magnet synchronous generator and battery storage device. The modulation of the DPI and the integrated BESS and WT maximum power point tracking control are presented and discussed. As proved by numerical simulations, the single-stage DPI can inject smooth electrical power into the grid at a unity power factor under highly variable speed conditions while always extracting the maximum power from the turbine.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine at Different Supply Voltage Levels
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Compact high torque/power density motors are needed for electrical vehicles in modern electric cars, this calls for effective temperature control of the electric motors. The voltage level in automotive spans a large range, usually between 96Vdc and 800Vdc, which asks for flexibility in the development of the powertrains in general, and of their electrical machines in particular. This paper's primary objective is to evaluate the thermal analysis of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous machine at different voltage levels of the power supply.

articleTitle: Model-driven development of a querying instrument for industrial PV inverters
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: For optimization of the monitoring and control of the PV on-grid inverters a model- driven engineering methodology have been applied to designing a software for querying the interface of the industrial inverters used for energy production from solar panels. Our proposed method is a key artifact in combining process, economical, and regulation implications. This alternative software has been designed for allowing local and centralized monitoring and control of the inverters. The architecture uses cloud- based standard data models for information exchanging, the database uses only 24 hours of historical data, and its main purpose is to synchronize produced power from different inverters, according with the amount of local loads demands. It is intended to be used in the smart grid implementation under the local regulation of countries. It has been tested under the ANRE (Romanian regulatory body) constraining rules, for two solar plants of 400 kW, and three different inverters.

articleTitle: Low-cost smarthome automation system for elderly
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper aims to present a low-cost system that can be implemented easily and can integrate multiple devices and automatic processes that help elderly people with daily activities and even monitor behavior. Using this system can help eliminate the need for Adult Foster Care for many people. It can be controlled remotely by the caregiver, so it also eliminates the transport to location necessity. Being able to define specific times for different activities, or even run commands automatically, it also reduces energy consumption.

articleTitle: Reviewing of different algorithms application with qualitative variables for the different financial indicators
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Nowadays the Machine Learning and Soft Computing algorithms are being deployed in different fields of applications and economy is one of them especially applied for decision making systems. The variables with their probabilistic values of their presence will be treated not like quantitative values but as qualitative ones. These linguistic variables are too near to human thinking where Fuzzy logic with its membership functions and as well combined with the application of the Boolean logic laws, all of them make it possible to construct a very accurate decision-making system. Decision making systems constructed by applying Fuzzy logic and Boolean laws can comply with trades fluctuations where uncertainty is quite common, and the business financial state as well is very unpredictable. These linguistic variables will be nothing less but the financial indicators of the small to medium businesses, where those are represented with linguistic variables with a probability of their values and appearance, and the decision for setting different weights to these indicators will help to create accurate economic models. Financial state of the firms we analyze is a multi-variable system and its variables are not simple numeric values, but they can be thought like analogue ones and by being like this those can reflect better the markets trend. The linguistic variables with multiple states that are studied come from the financial reports of the businesses and will undergo to different methods application like the DuPont, LA, LC [5]–[7].

articleTitle: The Impact of Three-Phase High Voltage Overhead Powerlines Characteristics on Electromagnetic Field Interference
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This study investigates the impact of three-phase powerline characteristics on electromagnetic field interferences prime magnetic field interferences. Electromagnetic fields generated by power transmission lines can have detrimental effects on nearby metallic structures, electronic devices, and human health. Understanding the relationship between powerline characteristics and electromagnetic interference is crucial for the development of effective mitigation strategies. To assess the effect of three-phase powerline characteristics on magnetic field interferences, the study presents a comprehensive set of numerical simulation studies based on the powerline configuration. The findings reveal that the arrangement of conductors, especially in proximity, number of circuits or phase transpositions can significantly influence the strength and spatial distribution of magnetic fields. Moreover, unbalanced loads can lead to increased asymmetry in the magnetic field, exacerbating interferences.

articleTitle: On the suitability of using ANSYS Motor-CAD software for teaching special electrical machines
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Special electrical machines are sophisticated electromagnetic devices in terms of both their design and behavior. As a result, their study is extensive and calls for a lot of multidisciplinary knowledge. The academic staff members who are participating in their teaching face a variety of educational difficulties as they work to ensure that the students fully comprehend all relevant matters. Modern teaching methods (also including distance learning) require advanced software tools to be used by the students. The ANSYS Motor-CAD software, which is frequently applied in the development of various electrical machine types, can also be used in higher education because it makes it simple to build interactive models of a wide range of electrical machines and because any changes made to the machine structures are immediately graphically displayed. With the aid of this flexible program, it is simple and accurate to conduct an electromagnetic analysis of the machines under investigation. The simulations also result in a wide range of electrical and mechanical properties for the examined electrical machines. The students may instantly see and feel the impacts of altering the topologies, as well as the various sizes and materials of the machines they are studying by utilizing this software program, which helps them comprehend their working principle and particular features. The easy-to-be-performed studies make it possible for electrical engineering students to improve their design abilities. The paper discusses two straightforward studies carried out utilizing the ANSYS Motor-CAD program. The emphasis is on how useful they are for B.Sc. electrical engineering students learning about special electrical machines.

articleTitle: Prerequisites of using similitude for studying distribution networks with a laboratory-scaled grid
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Analysis of static regimes distribution networks can be made by using power flow calculations. When real equipment behavior needs to be analyzed inside the grid, proper model of this device is needed for simulating it as well. However, full check might need either connection to the real grid, which may be not allowed in the grid operation, or other techniques may be used as well, e.g., hardware in the loop or down-scaled similar grids in a controlled lab environment. The simulation of a real distribution line through concentrated inductances and resistors avoids use of long cables if the laboratory solution is envisaged. Even so, the real impact in the grid can be better observed if the power of sources and of consumers are high enough for influencing the targeted grid. To avoid this difficult requirement, much smaller sources and consumers can be used if similitude is considered for dimensioning the laboratory network. The paper presents some introductory elements of the approach and shows by simulation that the effect on the lab-scaled grid is satisfactory similar with the results which may be obtained in a real grid, with higher involved powers. Moreover, it is shown that the similarity properties allow proper implementation of lab-scaled grids and the possibility to make analysis in a kW range, while the results can be more generally used, e.g., for hundreds of kW in a real microgrid.

articleTitle: A Q-Learning Based Approach For Voltage Control In Unbalanced Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In recent years, with the increasing use of renewable energy sources, voltage regulation in power distribution systems has become a greater challenge due to these sources’ intermittent and variable nature. To address this problem, this paper proposes a Q-learning-based method for voltage regulation in power distribution systems that incorporates tap changer voltage regulators when renewable energy sources are present. The voltage deviation problem is formulated as an optimization problem, and Q-learning is used to find near-optimal solutions that can effectively control voltage deviations and improve the overall performance of the power distribution system. The proposed method is applied to power distribution system using OpenDSS incorporated into Python. The simulations are performed on base case IEEE-123 Bus distribution network and with modifications by adding Photovoltaics. From the simulation results we observed that the proposed algorithm is able to solve the overvoltage and undervoltage problems.

articleTitle: Identifying the Potential of Consumer Back-up Generators to Cover the Balancing Energy Caused by Wind and Photovoltaic Sources
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In the absence of its own fossil fuel deposits, the Republic of Moldova intends to cover its electricity demand as much as possible by promoting renewable energy sources, especially after the energy crisis caused by the war in Ukraine. The realization of this idea would contribute not only to achieving decent energy security but also to the fulfillment of the country's commitments regarding greenhouse gas emissions reduction. Due to the lack of traditional sources for balancing the intermittency of energy produced by wind (WF) and photovoltaic (PV) sources, it becomes plausible to identify such capacities for country electricity consumers. The paper determines the potential capacity of the consumers’ backup generators (DG) to offset WF and PV intermittence; their competitiveness vis-à-vis other country plausible sources. The results obtained: 1. The identified country's power capacity potential of the backup generators is around 100MW. They may cover around 20% of the balancing energy needed in the 100%RES scenario; 2. For fuel prices recorded in 2020 and 2021, the application of DG to cover the balancing energy demand is more advantageous than the use of a Gas Turbine (GT). For 2022 fuel prices - GT; 3. To diminish needed balancing energy the optimal proportion between wind farms and photovoltaic capacities should be respected.

articleTitle: Training for Control Room Operators to Increase Local Renewable Energy Use in Neighboring Distribution Grids
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The European Union's carbon dioxide emission targets promote the necessary expansion of renewable generation plants. These large amounts of generation capacity at the lower voltage levels provide a steady increase in the times of the year when locally surplus energy is “pushed up” from the medium voltage level to the upper voltage levels. This places an additional load on the transmission grid, where the problems of grid congestion are currently seen in Germany. The project “Grid4Regio” has the goal increase the regional use of locally generated renewable energy and reduce the energy fed into the upper high voltage grid. In addition to the theoretical investigations, field tests were also carried out during the project. The new load cases in the distribution grids pose new challenges for the operators in the DSO control centers. In order to train these new scenarios safely and without risk, the grid control training simulator operated at the Darmstadt University of Applied Sciences was adapted and a suitable training program was developed.

articleTitle: Analysis of the modes of operation of an electric vehicle on energy consumption
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This manuscript presents a comprehensive analysis of the modes of operation of an electric vehicle (EV) and their impact on energy consumption. The study focuses on investigating the influence of three different drivers and three distinct road inclinations on the energy efficiency of an EV via simulation in MATLAB Simulink. The objective of this research is to gain a deeper understanding of the factors that affect energy consumption in various operational scenarios, ultimately contributing to the optimization of EV performance, range, and battery state of health (SOH). The obtained results (namely battery state of charge, battery current, motor torque) were analyzed in detail to assess the patterns associated with each driver type and road inclination scenario. Statistical techniques were employed to identify significant differences in energy efficiency among the various modes of operation. Additionally, insights were gained regarding the impact of driver behavior and road inclination on the EV's energy consumption.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Electromagnetic Disturbances between Single-Stage and Two-Stages AC/DC Boost Flyback Converters for LED Lighting Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: LEDs are gaining popularity in lighting systems because they are known for their dependable performance, extended lifespan, energy efficiency, and eco-friendliness. Nevertheless, these advantages attributed to the capabilities of LEDs are, in reality, achieved through the LED (driver and diode electroluminescent), which can be defined as the power supply that controls and ensures adequate light output from the LEDs. A static AC/DC converter based on rectifier diodes, and electronic switches, which are sources of harmonics and electromagnetic disturbances conducted respectively do this driving. In this paper, we simulate two LED driver topologies on LTspice software: single-stage AC/DC flyback boost, two-stage AC/DC flyback boost. The aim of this work is to evaluate the electromagnetic disturbances in common and differential modes and to compare the obtained results for the two topologies.

articleTitle: Digital Twin-based Decision-Making Methodology for the Optimal Operation of Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Digital Twin technology can potentially improve the security, control and resilience of the microgrids, considering a virtual model representation of each part integrated into an electrical power system. Using modern computing infrastructure based on faster real-time simulation, digital twins can allow a new approach to designing, operating and controlling microgrids. Thus, this paper presents a framework for adapting the digital twin in microgrid optimal operation based on a decision-making methodology for minimizing the power losses and improving the voltage magnitudes in microgrid nodes. The robustness of the methodology is tested in a rural microgrid to find the best operation strategy.

articleTitle: Applied data cleaning methods in outlier detection for residential consumer
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper is focusing on the topic of outlier detection methods applied to distinctive datasets encompassing residential energy consumption. In this research, we explore various approaches for outlier detection in data cleaning, including statistical, probabilistic and machine learning algorithms. The conclusion of the paper highlights the significance of detecting outliers for Romanian residential energy sector.

articleTitle: The influence of the distance between the transmitter and the receiver of a wireless power system on the coupling factor and the voltage induced
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The wireless power transfer systems are very often used to charge high-tech devices nowadays. To obtain a high performances wireless system it must be properly designed in order to have a power transfer from the emitter to the receiver as higher as possible taking into consideration all the specifications and parameters of the devices for which it is construct. This paper presents a way to optimize a wireless inductive power transfer system for the charging device. The physical limitations of the application require that the coils and electronic circuit be in optimal shape to maximize the output power delivered to the load and the power transmission efficiency of the wireless power system. The paper also includes numerical results for different working distances between the coils, ranging from 1 mm to 20 mm, and explores the response of the system at different frequencies.

articleTitle: Study on Non-Conformal Mesh Approach Applied on Layered Microelectronic Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Heater devices can have different shapes and sizes and can be made of different materials, such as polysilicon and metals. These structures are used for their fast and effective temperature control, thus overcoming the limitations of other heating methods. Poly heaters can be used for reliability purposes, degradation research, device characterization and overall development of microelectronic devices. In order to design these microelectronic structures and to overcome reliability and degradation issues, numerical simulation based on Finite Element Method is used. The application of FE non-conformal meshes allows concentrating the finer mesh in the zones of interest without impacting the mesh size in the other zones of structure of less interest. The use of non-conformal meshes leads to fewer elements, consequently reduced computational time. The paper proposes a methodology for setting the non-conformal mesh, consisting of (1) model partition, to allow the user a better control over the mesh density in areas of interest and (2) contact formulation. The results obtained on the computational model studied with conformal mesh, will act as a reference for further comparisons.

articleTitle: The Use Of Smith Diagram For Impedance Matching
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The main objective of this work is to learn the techniques of synthesis of adaptation circuits using both lumped components (for low frequencies) and exclusively transmission lines. Both the RL (return loss) value for the synthesized circuit and its quality factor Q can be calculated. It is also presented how the Smith diagram can be used in the calculation of the adaptation circuits of the signal transmission lines. Through the numerous examples of the use of the Smith chart in determining the circuit elements used in impedance matching, it confirms the great efficiency of this chart in the design of impedance matching schemes. For the calculation of the parameters of the lumped circuit elements, used in the impedance adaptation schemes for electric circuits and transmission lines, they were calculated, at each value of the operating frequency, by calling the MAPLE 18 program.

articleTitle: Reactive Power Compensation at Consumers Using Fuzzy Logic Control
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The research presented in this article had as objective to analyze how diverse types of fuzzy numbers, decision-making and defuzzification methods affect the efficiency of an FLC dedicated to reactive power compensation. The opening step of the research was to develop a model for the electricity consumer and determine the needs regarding the reactive power compensation. Next, the fuzzy logic controller is designed and diverse types of fuzzy numbers, decision-making and defuzzification methods are used, to decide upon the more appropriate ones. In the research MATLAB/Simulink and MATLAB/Fuzzy Logic Toolbox were employed to realize the simulations and testing of the fuzzy logic controller. The analysis uses twenty-four variants of the FLC, and the results show that the type of fuzzy sets affect the most the efficiency of the analyzed FLC.

articleTitle: Using infrared thermography for addressing the spatial variability of electromagnetic field in the proximity of emitting antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The spatial variability of electromagnetic field (EMF) in the proximity of two patch antennas operating at 3,5 GHz and 5,17 GHz was investigated by measuring the temperature of a thin liquid film placed near the transmitting antenna using an infrared camera. Measurements were performed for two types of signals: 1) continuous wave; 2) Long Term Evolution (LTE) signals of different bandwidths (5/10 MHz). An algorithm was designed to extract the maximum heating rate of the liquid, obtained when the effect of the thermal diffusion mechanism is minimal. This maximum heating rate is proportional to the internal electric field strength and thus the Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) value. A simulation was also performed to obtain the SAR distribution with comparative analysis of experimental and computational results. Our findings demonstrate the applicability of infrared thermography for EMF spatial mapping, highlighting the limitations of this measurement technique and providing preliminary insights on the difference between continuous wave and broadband signals like those emitted in modern communication standards.

articleTitle: Automatic Transfer Switch Application Controlled by PLC
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The purpose of the automatic transfer switching (ATS) is to swiftly replace the basic power supply with the standby power supply in the event of a loss or excessive reduction of the voltage in the primary power path, with simultaneous full efficiency of the back-up power supply devices. ATS automation is aimed at improving the reliability of the electricity supply. In this paper the authors present a hardware and software application used to study how to operate an ATS controlled by a PLC-HMI system, useful for engineers and master's students in the field of electrical engineering.

articleTitle: A LabVIEW Power Quality Analysis Application for a Three-phase Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The aim of the paper is to present a data acquisition measurement system and a power quality application developed in the LabVIEW programing environment, for a three-phase electrical system. The acquisition system complies of National Instruments acquisition module and Hall Effect transducers. The developed measuring and analysis system will be used for a future stand alone, low cost, three phase spectral analyzer, and as a didactical application for the laboratory classes in the signal processing discipline taught within the Faculty of Electrical Engineering of Cluj-Napoca. The proposed system will be composed of a three-phase consumer circuit in which the voltage and current of each phase will be acquired. To validate the date acquired and computed a three-phase power quality analyzer will be used. The application will provide the most important parameters in power quality: active, reactive and apparent power on each phase and total, the power factor on each phase and also the total power factor, the instantaneous and the rms values for the voltages and currents on each phase, the total harmonic distortion, the spectrum representation for each voltage and current acquired, the fundamental instantaneous and rms values for each voltage and current, the power factor for the fundamental components on each phase, the displacement angle between each voltage and current, and also the direct, invers and 0 components are computed and display.

articleTitle: Efficient Operation Approach of Microgrids Enriched with Prosumers and Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: When implementing the microgrid, electric energy consumption, energy storage, generation resources and plug-in electric vehicles should be managed and optimized in a way that lowers energy use, boosts efficiency, boost's reliability, and maintains security while meeting the rising demand at the lowest possible operating cost. As a result, utilities and researchers are paying more attention to energy management systems. In order to reduce losses from active or local electrical networks (microgrids) that have installed the smart metering system, this article presents a simulation algorithm based on calculations steady state iteratives to determine the best location for electrical energy storage systems at prosumers in a microgrid.

articleTitle: Smart Energy Communities - A Backbone for the Internet of Energy
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: One concept which is more and more promoted nowadays is the idea of combining decentralized renewable energy resources belonging to households into energy communities, which can be both controlled and coordinated by smart EMS systems. Due to their geographical particularities, rural and peri-urban areas can best accommodate such energy communities. If a community is large enough, power generation might be improved during the day when some PV panels could compensate any shading on other panels or maybe small wind turbines might add power during the night when solar energy is not available, but without controllable loads and battery energy storage systems (BESS), small communities comprised of buildings with PV generation and even small wind turbines might themselves become a source of significant variability. This paper will propose a model to combine PV energy production with storage and controllable loads in smart energy communities, aggregated on a smart EMS platform (Smart Control Hub Energy Data Aggregation Platform - SCHEEDAP) in order to enable the community to use a large portion of its electric energy consumption from its own renewable energy production, while also decreasing their energy costs. The case study presented is showing how the use of renewable energy assets together with storage systems for rural energy communities might lead to the decrease in power consumption from the grid and will help the distribution grid to be more reliable and secure. Using distributed energy assets in smart energy communities, controlled by an aggregation platform with EMS functionality and being able to distribute active power reference set-points to each household's local controller based on close to real-time optimization results, creates the premises not only for local self-consumption and decrease of energy costs for the community, but will also constitute a backbone for the Internet of Energy at the community's level.

articleTitle: Identification of Parameters and Power Losses of Six-Phase Asynchronous Machines by Induction Regenerative Method
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The work is focused on identifying the equivalent circuit parameters and power losses of a six-phase asynchronous motor with the cage rotor, using a laboratory bench with an adjustable three-phase power supply and without mechanical load. For asynchronous machines, the induction method with recovery was adapted, according to which one three-phase system of the six-phase stator winding is energised and operates in motor mode. The second three-phase system works in generator mode, idling or short-circuited. With theoretical arguments, an equivalent scheme of the six-phase motor in induction mode with recovery was proposed. The methodology for identifying the parameters of the equivalent scheme and the constant and additional power losses of the six-phase asynchronous motor was developed. Multiple experimental measurements confirmed the correctness of the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Optimizing the operation of established renewable energy storage systems using artificial intelligence
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper explores the use of artificial intelligence (AI) for optimizing the operation of energy storage systems obtained from renewable sources. After presenting the theoretical foundations of renewable energy, energy storage, and AI optimization algorithms, the paper focuses on how AI can be applied to improve the efficiency and performance of energy storage systems. Existing case studies are analyzed to highlight the advantages and challenges of using AI in this context. Ultimately, this paper concludes that using AI for optimizing renewable energy storage systems is a promising method to enhance efficiency and contribute to the transition to a low-carbon economy.

articleTitle: FPGA based Real-Time simulation of FlyBack converter using graphical programming tools
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper presents a novel FPGA Real-Time simulation solution based on modern graphical programming and automated testing tools. The proposed setup was used for simulation of high-speed power electronics switching phenomenon within some considered circuit topologies. In the actual setup, the behavior of a power electronic converter stage was hardware - emulated using a powerful FPGA (Field Programmable Gate-Array) logic processing unit. This logic - processor unit was used to run fast, and intensive computing tasks related to the desired power electronics circuit topology behavioral simulation techniques. The FPGA unit was equipped with analog and digital input and output ports, so that the resultant digital real-time simulation waveforms were physically generated as variable voltage signals. The real variable voltage signals required in the control scheme of the considered power electronics topology were also acquired using the built-in digital and analog ports. The physical control variable voltage signal was generated using a digital control law algorithm implemented within an embedded system process controller (NI MyRIO). This kind of simulation approach is so-called Hardware in the Loop (HIL) Real-Time simulation. This simulation technique requires two real-time computing systems, the HIL simulation computer (NI PXI) and the embedded controller (NI MyRIO). As software infrastructure, specialized real-time simulation and automated testing software environments were used. The whole presented HIL solution is mainly centered on the National Instruments devices plus the Lab VIEW software infrastructure and also the VeriStand test automation environment including the OPAL-RT eHS circuit solver Add-on. Matlab - Simulink was also used to implement the power electronics circuit model. The overall system represents a Hardware In the Loop and Virtual Instrumentation Engineering Workbench solution.

articleTitle: System Development- Major Changes Needs. Power Quality Importance
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The global concern about climate change forced policy makers for new strategies for decarbonisation. Europe is the world champion with(55% in 2030 and 100 % in 2050 targets. Coal, some nuclear and gaspower plants in the next steps, are going to be decommissioned. New developments in generation technologies (small and large scale) are expected to be deployed on large scale. Efficiency and quality in all power sector is expected to increase. This paper presents tendency in power sector and the increasing role of power quality. Renewable generation, integrated power markets, digitization, the conservation and efficiency use of electricity are included in R&D projects and are coming daily in our life. Traditional way of project promotion based on fesability study is obsolete. Some steps in order to evaluate the social benefit are introduced by different CBA (Cost Based Analise) which are trying to monetize social benefit like green gase reduction and creation of skills to the people. Generally speaking, distributed generation looks to be in conflict with global transmission grid. The scope of this paper is to prove, one more time that electricity is one key driver for social development and this is the place for large but also small scale projects. Also, this should be in line with quantity and power quality needed.

articleTitle: Forecasting the electricity balance of a small manufacturer with photovoltaic production using machine learning
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Implementing photovoltaic production capacity at industrial sites is a step forward for smart-grid technologies by enabling improved energy efficiency. The biggest challenge for every renewable energy producer is unpredictability. This paper presents an industry case study and the necessity of energy balance forecasting. Lower forecast errors can improve supply-consumption balance by offering precise information for participating in the power market. Forecasting hourly energy consumption and production of an industrial consumer is difficult because of the high volatility for both processes that need to be independently analyzed. The present paper aims to offer a detailed analysis of the efficiency of algorithms applied to industry data for forecasting the electricity balance, which can help the effectiveness of renewable energy installed at industrial sites. The exogenous variables used in forecasting methods, among others, are temperature, solar irradiation, and cloudiness. Implemented machine learning algorithms for forecasting: Multi-Layer Perceptron and Recurrent Neural Networks, and a traditional Multiple Regression algorithm.

articleTitle: Optimal Solutions Identification for Horizontal Earth Grounding, With Pipe Type Electrodes
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The main purpose of the work is to identify the optimal domains for the earth grounding with horizontal, pipe-type electrodes. This continues a previous work, which summarizes the problem of horizontal earth grounding, brings together the calculation relationships for their design sizes and presents the optimal applicable criteria. The contributions of the present research begin with the framing of the earth grounding in the more general case of the penetration of the electromagnetic field in massive conductors, which is why the depth of penetration of the electromagnetic field in the main types of soils is determined. The relatively small dimensions of the earth groundings in relation to the penetration depth are noted, but they also warn against the existence of possible obstructions. The optimal criteria, i.e. minimum in this case, are the area of the footprint on the ground, the total mass of the metallic materials and the investment costs with the earth grounding. Their application on the physical model of the horizontal earth groundings, led to the identification of optimal domains, bipolarly grouped at the smaller dimensions of the electrode lengths, but at the lower and upper limits of the distances between the electrodes respectively.

articleTitle: Next Generation RES-based student residence. A case study
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The demand for sustainable and energy-efficient buildings led to an increased focus on the use of renewable energy sources in the construction industry. This article presents a case study of a (next-generation) student residence building (SRB), that could integrate generation from photovoltaic (PV) panels with flexibility in operation given by a battery energy storage sys-tem (BESS). The studied RES-based SRB is designed to provide a comfortable living environment while minimizing energy use and carbon emissions. In this paper, the design and implementation of the proposed generation system, including the selection of the PV technology and the battery storage system, both based on high-reporting rate measurement information is discussed. The energy transfer of the system based on instrumentation values provided by a smart-metering infrastructure from the campus grid is analyzed also by performing digital real-time simulations. This study provides insights into the design and construction of future sustainable and energv-efficient buildings.

articleTitle: Grid support by BESS. Benefits for a Solar Thermal Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: During the last decades, battery energy storage systems (BESS) plants have received a growing interest due to appearance of applications supporting the stabilization of the power grid and improving both the performance and revenues for renewable energy sources, such as photovoltaic (PV), concentrated thermal solar (CSP) and wind plants. The integration of the emerging grid disruptive technologies, such as renewable energy sources (RES) and electric vehicles (EVs) destabilize the power grid. Energy storage solutions are now commonly available. For instance, Li-ion manufacturers offer relatively reliable and economic residential battery solutions. BESS technology can support the power grid stabilization through frequency regulation (FR), auto voltage regulation (AVR), peak shaving and other applications, more efficiently and less expensive than the common practice technology used today as capacitors banks and synchronous generators. The paper aims to highlight engineering considerations on BESS technologies design for grid support applications, to more efficient use of renewable energy plants in the context of current and future considerations related to global economy and deep decarbonization of the grids. The work presents a technical-economic analysis based on a project of adding BESS to an existing solar thermal plant, in order to load leveling. The background is related exclusively to the context of the US energy market, as the CSP is subjected to.

articleTitle: Dynamic Modeling and Analysis of VSC-HVDC Links in Large AC Networks using EUROSTAG Software
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The following paper is dedicated to developing and calibrating a dynamic and steady-state VSC - HVDC (Voltage Source Converter - High Voltage Direct Current) model suitable for large AC (Alternating Current) networks by using SmartFlow and EUROSTAG software. In order to simulate the dynamic behavior, a steady-state Test Network with a large number of AC nodes and a VSC-HVDC bipolar link with a total capacity of 2000 MW, is created using SmartFlow software. The dynamic behavior of the VSC-HVDC model is analyzed using EUROSTAG software under different fault types in the network. The dynamic tests evaluate the voltage and frequency stability of the system, as well as the LVRT (Low Voltage Ride Through) capabilities of the VSC-HVDC link against the requirements of international and national legislations such as EU 2016/1447 Commission Regulation code and the National Grid Code of the Romanian TSO (Transmission System Operator) as well as ANRE order 185/2019. Additional simulations are conducted for the active and reactive power response of the VSC-HVDC links to analyze the converter's capability to respond to a change in active or reactive power setpoints. The study results show that the proposed, calibrated VSC-HVDC dynamic model functions properly in a large AC network and meets the technical legislation requirements of the Romanian National Power System. The developed VSC - HVDC model could serve as a starting point for future developments of the dynamic simulation model used by the TSO for a large AC network.

articleTitle: NZEB compliance principles in Romania for residential buildings
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Energy efficiency is one of the solutions to reduce greenhouse gases (GHG) emissions. In the building sector, one of the world's main polluters, the concepts of Nearly Zero Energy Buildings (NZEB) and Zero Energy Buildings (ZEB) have emerged in order to meet the environmental and climate targets for 2030 and 2050. The paper studies the NZEB concept, the criteria for meeting the standard in buildings, the legislation at European level and specifically on the envelope side of the residential building, analyzing for several types of insulation materials whether or not they meet the standards.

articleTitle: Analysis of the risks and identification of the mitigation measures for the energy transition investment projects in Turkey and Vietnam
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This research paper explores the risks and mitigation strategies associated with energy transition investment projects in Turkey and Vietnam. The study focuses on understanding the changing energy balance in these countries and the role of multilateral organizations in financing renewable energy initiatives. The analysis identifies the main risks in each country, including economic, institutional, and governance effectiveness, financial system, payment culture, and rule-of-law risks. It examines Turkey and Vietnam's specific challenges and opportunities, considering economic stability, political environment, financial sector risks, and adherence to regulatory frameworks. The study concludes by providing recommendations for companies planning energy transition investment projects in Turkey and Vietnam. It suggests incorporating the costs of risk mitigation instruments into the financial analysis and utilizing the mechanisms provided by multilateral agencies for effective risk management. The findings aim to guide decision-makers and investors in understanding the risks and implementing appropriate strategies to ensure the success of renewable energy projects in these countries.

articleTitle: Hybrid Machining Performances: A state-of-the-art review
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Additive manufacturing procedures are proven technologies to produce highly complex metals and plastic parts. The technology known as hybrid machining (HM) combines two or more machining processes into a single operation. The consequence of this technique is an improvement in efficiency, accuracy, and surface finish. This article presents a comprehensive analysis of the performance of the hybrid machining process and design principles. Based on the classification of the processes, will be provided also a description of various productivity improvements. The evaluation examines the technology's advantages and disadvantages, how performance is impacted by process factors, and potential applications in various industries. The findings of this study will be very useful to researchers and those who operate in the hybrid machining industry.

articleTitle: Synchronous Power Transfer to Induction Motors Operating with Variable Frequency Drives Case 1: Residual Voltage and Fixed Time Transfer
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The synchronous transfer is an exact procedure that allows one variable frequency drive (VFD) to operate multiple motors for process control. The paper analyses the function of synchronous transfer for utilization with variable frequency drives commonly used in pumping applications within the pipeline industry. There are three directions subject to study and testing: the equipment with synchronous transfer capabilities, different types of transfer available, and considerations regarding the safety of the operation. The experimental part of the project consists of assembling a system that assures the induction motors' transfer to and from a variable frequency drive as desired, a transient process that must not disturb the overall system significantly. Switching logic is handled by a Programmable Logic Controller (PLC). Waveforms captured of the system operating at specific times certify that the induction motor transfer occurs safely.

articleTitle: Hydrogen Storage Potential of the Graphitic Carbon Nitride
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The size of the global market of renewable energy has increased significantly in the last years, thanks to new environmental policies that were adopted to slow down the inevitable rise of global temperatures. In this article the focus in on addressing hydrogen storage, that is acceptable for the environment and for security reasons. Today's methods of storing H<inf>2</inf> that are viable for economic use are liquid hydrogen (LH2) and compressed hydrogen, however, they present some risks that other experimental methods do not have. For example, liquid hydrogen can ignite and burn in the presence of oxygen, and it can also create an explosive mixture with air if it evaporates too quickly. The main topic of the research is the study of the economic possibilities of integration of the Graphitic Carbon Nitride g-C3N4, into existing H<inf>2</inf> storage systems and the study of the prospects of creating a new scalable system using Graphitic Carbon Nitride as the base material for storage possibly at Standard Temperature and Pressure (STP). This study aims to make an analysis of the newly proposed system and to compare its general storage possibilities to already-in-use solutions, as a reference to other hydrides.

articleTitle: Equipment Parameter Investigation for a Proposed Power Conductor Hot Spot Identification system
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Reliability, efficiency and continuity of power energy supplied is an area which receives increasing attention as the main infrastructure of power transmission and distribution systems in many countries is ageing. Hot spot related cable failures and power interruptions have a big financial impact on the power provider. The operational parameters of a method to identify in real time hot spots on cables is investigated in this paper, which can result to timely fault prevention. This can be achieved through exploiting the optical sensing capabilities of the existing optical fibre on-grid network. The resulting parameters aim to be advantageous for the system as they increase accuracy and will enable the Remote, automated, continuous, and real time monitoring of the grid infrastructure integrity.

articleTitle: Power systems resilience against cyber-attacks. A systematic analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Power outages can have serious consequences for national security and a country's economy. Today, electricity generation, transmission and distribution rely on digital systems such as computer systems and communication networks. This development introduces new vulnerabilities in the reliability of electricity supply due to cyber-attacks on information and communication systems. Cyber-attacks evolve from insignificant crime to state-sponsored cyber terrorism. This paper provides a systemic analysis of the most relevant cyber security studies that address the power systems resilience to cyber-attacks. Research that defines cyber security risks and studies that develop solutions to improve the security of power systems are reviewed. Publications between 2013 and 2023 have been reviewed and quantitatively evaluated, contributing to the identity and evaluation of studies developments over the past ten years. The paper additionally proposes an evaluation of a reference attack, the only one executed in 2015 in Ukraine, which caused energy outages for nearly 225,000 clients in western Ukraine. Data about the target of the attack, the method of attack, the purpose, the result obtained by the attackers, the consequences of the attack are documented. After the analysis of this security incident on the power system in Ukraine, a series of measures meant to prevent this type of attacks are going to be proposed.

articleTitle: Modeling and simulating solar and renewable energy systems using artificial intelligence
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper explores how artificial intelligence can be used to model and simulate renewable solar energy systems. With the expansion of the use of renewable energy, solar energy systems have become a popular and promising option for electricity generation. However, modeling and simulating these systems can be difficult and expensive. Therefore, this paper analyzes the use of artificial intelligence to improve the process of modeling and simulating renewable solar energy systems. It presents the basic principles of renewable solar energy systems and artificial intelligence, as well as the algorithms and techniques used for modeling and simulating these systems. In addition, the paper focuses on data collection and processing, and the results obtained through simulations are analyzed and compared with other electric power generation systems. The conclusions drawn in this paper suggest that the use of artificial intelligence can improve the performance of renewable solar energy systems and reduce the costs and effort required for modeling and simulating these systems.

articleTitle: SPICE model of a “n” channel MOSFET transistor
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In this paper, starting from a new equivalent circuit of a real n-channel MOS-FET transistor realized based on principle of operation and considering the information from datasheet, a new SPICE model is created, where the drain-source resistance of the transistor varies with base-source voltage and with temperature. To verify the accuracy of the SPICE model, a comparison of the SPICE model of a n-channel MOS-FET with the behavior of the real MOS-FET and with the SPICE behavior of the MOS-FET proposed by the component manufacturer will be performed. Validation of the model is performed at a temperature of −40°C, 25°C and 125°C. The following parameters of the “n” channel MOS-FET transistor are validated: parasitic capacitance from the gate, ON time, RISE time, OFF time, FALL time, the drain-source loss current, drain-source breakdown voltage, gate-source breakdown voltage and drain-source resistance.

Author Keywords: the equivalent circuit for a real MOSFET transistor

articleTitle: On the Mitigation of Renewable Energy Curtailment by Using Pumped Hydro Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: To increase the penetration of renewable energy sources into electrical systems, it is essential to lessen renewable energy curtailment. Pumped Hydro Storage (PHS) systems are a promising alternative to achieve lower curtailment rates. This work analyses the effect of a PHS system in an electrical network regarding renewable energy curtailment behaviour. The analysis is addressed through an optimal power flow formulation to minimize power loss while satisfying operating and renewable energy curtailment constraints. Preliminary results for a modified IEEE 14-bus test feeder suggested that implementing the PHS decreased transmission losses by 2.2% and mitigated 16.8% of curtailed renewable energy for whole- year simulations.
